defect.description: The backward-incompatible crash: kwargs.pop('method', form.method).upper() raises AttributeError when a caller passes method=None explicitly, which used to work (Request turns a None method into GET); the change should treat None like a missing method.

review_items: from_form .upper() crashes with AttributeError when method=None passed explicitly (backward-incompatible)
from_form .upper() crashes when form.method is None and no method kwarg passed
valid_form_methods is a mutable class-level list; use tuple/frozenset
Redundant uppercase in from_form duplicates Request.__post_init__ normalization
votes.evidence_quote: `kwargs.pop("method", form.method).upper()` raises `AttributeError` when the caller explicitly passes `method=None`.
votes.justification: The review's first finding names the exact defect at from_form. It identifies the AttributeError on an explicit method=None and explains that the code previously worked because Request normalized None to GET.
